findings.title: The +2 'signal-confluence ≥4 (second-agent confirmation)' line is a literal re-count of already-scored quantities, and the same composite is leveraged FOUR times in one decision chain
findings.where: daily-analysis.md Step 0 #3/#6, Step 3, Step 3a, Step 4 line '+2 uw insights signal-confluence ≥4'; weekly-analysis.md Step 0 #6, Step 3, Step 3a, Step 4; signal-confluence-quant.md LB-gate list item 5
findings.evidence: Live probe `uw insights signal-confluence --help`: "Score tickers by alignment of bullish/bearish factors across screener + dark pool + OI + IV." Live sample (`--json --quiet --top-n 3`) returns per-ticker `"factors": ["bullish_flow", "low_pcr", "volume_spike", "dp_accumulation", "oi_building", "low_iv_cheap_options"]` — `dp_accumulation` ↔ the +3 accumulation line, `oi_building` ↔ the +1/+3 oi-trend line, `bullish_flow` ↔ the +1 cum-premium-flow line. The composite is used at: (1) Step 0 funnel/anchor — "`uw insights signal-confluence` (`min_score=3`, top 25 each direction) — multi-factor scoring; agents start their hunts here" plus `uw playbook daily-synthesis --help`: "Morning briefing: market regime + top bullish/bearish confluence + watchlist alerts"; (2) Step 3 entry gate — "one Phase 1 agent flags it AND `uw insights signal-confluence` rates it ≥4"; (3) Step 4 — "+2 uw insights signal-confluence ≥4 (second-agent confirmation)"; (4) Step 3a — "`uw insights signal-confluence` (second-agent confirmation — added 2026-05-23 P0.2 ... LOAD-BEARING)" as 1 of the 3-of-5 gate tools.
findings.why_it_matters: A name that already earned +3 accum, +1 OI-build, +1 cum-flow has, by construction, ≥3 of the composite's 6 factors lit — the +2 'confirmation' is near-deterministic, not independent. Calling it 'second-agent confirmation' is actively misleading: it is the same tape data re-aggregated server-side. The Phase-4 '+19.5pp marginal' that justified adding it is selection-confounded (candidates are funnel-seeded and gate-admitted on the same score). Net effect: +2 of essentially free points pushes correlated single-footprint names over the HIGH ≥9 cut, and the same score simultaneously satisfies entry and the LB demotion gate, so no layer of the chain can catch it.
findings.confidence: high — factor list verified live; would soften only if the server-side factor definitions used data lineages disjoint from the rubric tools (the help text and factor names say otherwise)

findings.title: One institutional actor's footprint can earn ~13/14 available daily points (16 weekly) and trivially satisfies the 3-of-5 LB gate 5-of-5 — HIGH tier is reachable from a single market event
findings.where: daily-analysis.md Step 4 rubric + Step 3a; weekly-analysis.md Step 4 + Step 3a; signal-confluence-quant.md LB-gate list
findings.evidence: Mapping each scored line to its market quantity: +3 accumulation (the actor's DP prints + opened OI + ask-side volume: `uw oi smart-positioning --help` = "Cross-reference OI changes with ask/bid volume"; `uw dark-pool block-stratified --help` = "Per-ticker DP premium stratified into mega/block/large/retail tiers"), +1 oi-trend ("OI buildup or decline" — the same opens), +1 cum-premium-flow ("Sum bullish/bearish premium" — the same prints), +2 signal-confluence (factors `dp_accumulation`+`oi_building`+`bullish_flow`+`low_pcr`, all moved by the same actor), +3 DEX flip (`uw options-structure dex --help`: "Net dealer delta hedge — positive = call-heavy public, dealer hedge BUYS underlying" — the dealer's mechanical response to the actor's own option buys), +2 multileg (the actor executing via spreads), +1 sector leader (conditions (b)/(c) are the actor's own `cum_premium_flow_30d` again). Daily total = 13 vs HIGH ≥9; the minimal core accum+OI+cum_flow+confluence+DEX = 10. Weekly: +3 OI + +3 accum + +2 rolls + +1 cum_flow + +2 confluence + +2 DEX + +2 multileg-repeat + +1 sector = 16. All five Step 3a LB tools (block-stratified, cum-premium-flow, institutional-accumulation, DEX, signal-confluence) are downstream of the identical footprint — the breadth gate measures tool citations, not actor/quantity independence.
findings.why_it_matters: The rubric's additivity assumes component independence (the Bailey & López de Prado point the C11 note itself cites). One whale building one position fires sweeps→OI→premium→DP→DEX→confluence as a causal cascade, manufacturing HIGH-tier 'confluence' from a single bet. The C2 market-excess gate caps the *size* of beta-longs at half, but tier assignment, Executive-Summary placement, watchlist write-back, and deep-dive hand-off all key on the raw additive score — those channels remain uncontained. Assumptions flagged: the DEX-flip and sector-persistence contributions require the actor to be large relative to the name's book (realistic for the mega-cap names this fleet surfaces); the +2 multileg requires spread execution.
findings.confidence: high on the mapping (tool semantics verified live); medium on the exact 13/16 maximum (DEX/sector lines depend on actor size vs total book — but even the conservative 10-point core clears HIGH)

findings.title: Weekly confluence threshold drift: entry gate ≥5, rubric +2 line ≥4, quant told to query min_score=5 — and the tool has no per-ticker mode at all
findings.where: weekly-analysis.md Step 3, Step 3 note, Step 4 line '+2 ... ≥4 at WEEK_END', Step 2a; daily-analysis.md Step 2a; uw CLI flag set
findings.evidence: Weekly Step 3: "one Phase 1 agent flags it AND `uw insights signal-confluence` rates it ≥5 at WEEK_END ... Note: the threshold here is `≥ 5` (vs `≥ 4` in `/daily-analysis`) because weekly recommendations carry more capital and need a stricter prior." Weekly Step 4 rubric: "+2 uw insights signal-confluence ≥4 at WEEK_END (second-agent confirmation)". Weekly Step 2a: "Run `uw insights signal-confluence` per ticker (`min_score=5` for weekly)". Live `--help` shows flags are only `--date, --direction, --min-score, --top-n` — there is no `--symbol`/ticker flag; it is a top-N screener, not a per-ticker scorer.
findings.why_it_matters: Three contradictions stack: (a) a weekly name entering via the 1-agent path needs ≥5 and therefore automatically earns the +2 (≥4) line — definitional, not confirmatory (same definitional auto-award exists daily where gate and rubric are both ≥4); (b) a name scoring exactly 4 is filtered out of a min_score=5 query, so the ≥4 award is undecidable as instructed; (c) "run per ticker" is unimplementable — the quant can only check membership of a top-N ranked list, so any candidate outside the returned top-25 silently reads as no-confluence (or the agent improvises with a larger top-n), making both the gate and the +2 line non-deterministic across runs.
findings.confidence: high — all three texts quoted verbatim and the flag set verified live

findings.title: Dead-letter rubric deduction lines: −3 regime-conflict and −1/−2 corr-cluster are 'applied in 2d' as score points, but neither Phase-2 agent is permitted to apply them — and risk-monitor applies tier cuts for the same facts anyway
findings.where: daily-analysis.md Step 4 lines '−1 risk-monitor flags in correlation cluster ... applied in 2d on top of raw score' and '−3 uw risk market-regime conflicts ... applied in 2d'; weekly-analysis.md Step 4 '−2 ... applied in 2d' and '−3 WoW ... applied in 2d'; signal-confluence-quant.md; risk-monitor.md sizing rule
findings.evidence: Daily Step 2a: "**The quant does not gate on regime/correlation** — that's risk's job in 2d." risk-monitor.md: "Do **not** override the quant's score; only size around it" — its mechanism is tiers: "−1 tier if regime conflicts with direction ... −1 tier if member of a corr-cluster (pairwise corr ≥ 0.70)". Yet the rubrics list these as score components inside "Daily conviction score = Σ:" (−3/−1 daily, −3/−2 weekly), and the envelope invariant is "Σ score_components[].points == raw_score for every call (the quant already guarantees this — the validator enforces it)" — raw_score is frozen at quant emission.
findings.why_it_matters: Either the point-deductions never fire (the quant is forbidden, risk-monitor can't touch the score, the validator locks the sum) — in which case the published rubric overstates its own regime/correlation discipline and every embedded-rubric audit reads phantom protections — or an implementer applies both the points and the tier cut, double-penalizing one fact through two units. Bonus inconsistency: the corr penalty is −1 (daily) vs −2 (weekly) vs '−1 tier' (risk-monitor) — three magnitudes/units for the identical market fact.
findings.confidence: high on the textual contradiction; medium on which branch real runs take (would resolve by reading produced decision.json envelopes, which sit outside this lens's quarantine-safe scope)

findings.title: OI-build is scored three times weekly: +3 standalone, again inside the +3 accumulation conjunction, again inside the confluence `oi_building` factor — and the daily demote rationale (+1 because 'correlated with the LOAD-BEARING components') was never propagated to the weekly rubric
findings.where: weekly-analysis.md Step 4 lines '+3 uw historical oi-trend BUILDING for the full week' and '+3 3+ aligned signals in accumulation-hunter'; daily-analysis.md Step 4 '+1 multi-day OI build' comment
findings.evidence: Daily rubric: "+1 multi-day OI build (uw historical oi-trend BUILDING, --days ≥ 5) # was +2; reduced 2026-05-09 (Phase 4 +5pp marginal — supportive, not load-bearing; **correlated with the LOAD-BEARING components above**)". (DP + **OI** + uw oi smart-positioning ...)" — whose aligned-signal set includes the same OI build, and whose `oi smart-positioning` input is per `--help` "Cross-reference **OI changes** with ask/bid volume". The confluence +2 line's live factor list also contains `oi_building`. Weekly's +2 `uw oi position-rolls` is a fourth OI-change expression for LEAP names.

The system already diagnosed exactly this correlation on the daily side in 2026-05-09 and fixed only one of the two files.
findings.confidence: high — all texts verbatim; the smart-positioning and confluence lineages verified by live --help/sample

findings.title: cum_premium_flow_30d is one scalar driving five scoring mechanisms — a passing flow pays twice and unlocks a third line (+4-point swing from one datum); C11 explicitly blesses the stack
findings.where: daily/weekly Step 4 (+3 accum conjunction condition, +1 cum_flow line, +1 sector-leader conditions (b)(c), −3/−1 flow_conflict); signal-confluence-quant.md 'Conditional dark_pool_accumulation conjunction' + 'Do not route around the gate' + Ties rule
findings.evidence: C11: "full +3 only when cum_premium_flow_30d confirms (sign aligned with thesis AND |cum_flow_30d| ≥ $50M); else halved (floored) +3→+1". Cum-flow line: "+1 uw historical cumulative-premium-flow shows net directional accretion". Sector line: "(b) cum_premium_flow_30d direction aligned ... AND (c) |cum_flow_30d| ≥ $50M". The anti-routing rule only blocks the FAILING case: "a flow that fails this conjunction gate ... does not qualify ... for the +1 cum_flow line either" — when the flow PASSES, the same ≥$50M aligned reading awards the marginal +2 on the accumulation line, +1 on its own line, and +1 on the sector line simultaneously. It is also the flow_conflict deduction input and the tie-breaker ("rank ties by cum_premium_flow_30d magnitude"). Live `--help`: "Sum bullish/bearish premium across recent N sessions" — and the audit annotation on the +1 line itself says the tool is "NO-INFO across three consecutive path-aware audits (−3.5pp MC)".
findings.why_it_matters: A 4-point swing (roughly the HIGH−MED gap plus one) rides on a single measurement the system's own audits grade as no-information standalone. The C11 'conjunction' also doesn't buy actor-independence: the confirming premium flow is causally the same institution's prints that generated the DP/OI signals being confirmed — it confirms venue-consistency, not a second opinion. C11 fixed the false-HIGH on flow-unconfirmed accumulation but concentrated single-datum leverage in the confirmed case.
findings.confidence: high — texts verbatim; the −3.5pp MC characterization is the file's own annotation

findings.title: Risk-monitor re-penalizes facts already deducted upstream: one adverse-flow read can cost −3 points (quant) + −1 tier (adverse sector) + −1 tier (debate, with the bear literally handed the same score_components); a CAUTION fundamentals fact has two channels
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md 'Mechanical flow_conflict deduction'; risk-monitor.md tool item 6, sizing-rule lines for sector/debate/fundamentals; daily-analysis.md Step 2c
findings.evidence: Quant: "When the candidate's cum_premium_flow_30d direction contradicts the inferred trade direction ... you MUST apply a numeric deduction to raw_score" (−3/−1). risk-monitor: "−1 tier if sector rotation flowing out of the name's sector with persistence_score ≥ 0.6" — sector-flow-persistence is the same net-option-premium quantity aggregated to GICS, so a name whose own outflow dominates its sector read is hit twice on one flow. Debate channel: Step 2c "Hand both sides: the ticker's `score_components`, the Step 2b fundamentals enrichment, and the Step 0 macro/event context", then risk-monitor: "−1 tier if bear residual ≥ bull residual (debate did not clear the trade)" — the bear's case is constructed from the very components the quant already deducted, so the same flow conflict can drive a third penalty. Fundamentals: "−1 tier if fundamentals_verdict == CAUTION" while the same CAUTION facts feed the bear's residual. No de-duplication rule exists anywhere in risk-monitor.md (the only mutual-exclusivity rule in the system is between flow_conflict and flow_conflict_lite at the quant).
findings.why_it_matters: Penalty-side double-counting is less dangerous than award-side (it biases toward skipping, not toward bad fills), but it distorts measured calibration: gated-call realized rates get compared against gates that fire 2–3× per underlying fact, making individual gates look uninformative (the file's own event-risk note records a 90%-firing/zero-discrimination episode of exactly this 'haircut, not filter' failure). It also asymmetrically taxes flow-based shorts/fades — the side the 2026-05-30 annotation says carries the desk's actual +20pp alpha.
findings.confidence: medium-high — the channel topology is verbatim; whether the debate gate actually re-fires on quant-deducted facts in practice depends on bear-agent behavior (would confirm by reading produced envelopes' gate_verdicts, outside this lens's file scope)

findings.title: The confluence composite is magnitude-blind and floor-blind: binary factor counting admits $10K net flow and sub-$5 names — yet +2 points, the entry gate, and an LB-gate slot ride on its threshold
findings.where: uw insights signal-confluence live output; daily-analysis.md Step 3/Step 4; signal-confluence-quant.md LB gate
findings.evidence: Live sample: DNUT scores 5 with `"close": 4.2` (below the C12 $5 floor), `"net_flow": 10077` ($10K 'bullish_flow'); BLSH scores 5 with `"net_flow": 47500` and `"volume_ratio": 0.23` (a fifth of normal volume still earns 5 factors). The score is an unweighted count of 6 binary factors with no magnitude or liquidity weighting; ≥4 of 6 is the bar that pays +2 and admits 1-agent candidates.
findings.why_it_matters: C12 flooring at Step 0 protects the funnel, but the quant's per-ticker re-check, the entry gate, and the LB-gate citation all consume the raw composite score, whose 'alignment' can be six trivial readings. A 6-factor name with $250K of net flow (SBUX in the live sample) outranks a 3-factor name with $100M behind it — the opposite of how a desk weights evidence. This degrades both the +2 line's information content and the LB gate's discriminating power.
findings.confidence: high — observed directly in the live sample

findings.title: Internal sign contradiction: the confluence factor `low_pcr` rewards exactly the crowding the contrarian −2 line penalizes; plus residual hygiene drift (sub-0.50 sizing daily 'starter/skip' vs weekly '×0 watch-only'; risk-monitor's signal-class vocabulary doesn't match the quant's)
findings.where: signal-confluence live factors vs daily/weekly Step 4 '−2 contrarian-scanner ... rising pc-ratio-zscore'; daily Step 5 vs weekly Step 5 tables; risk-monitor.md inputs vs signal-confluence-quant.md class labels
findings.evidence: Live factors include `"low_pcr"` (bullish credit for a low put/call ratio) while the rubric carries "−2 contrarian-scanner flags as overcrowded long with rising uw historical pc-ratio-zscore" — the same P/C quantity earns a share of +2 in one line and −2 in another on the same crowded-long name, partially netting the contrarian's only penalty. Daily Step 5: "< 0.50 | starter / skip"; weekly Step 5: "< 0.50 | × 0 (drop to watch-only regardless of conviction tier)" — same win-rate, different floors. risk-monitor.md expects classes "sweep / accumulation / gamma_breakout / leap_oi_build / earnings_vol / multileg / fade ..." while the quant emits "dark_pool_accumulation | multi_day_sweep | oi_build | leap_directional | multileg_directional ..." — drift in the keys mechanical gates (C4 on bullish_flow/bearish_flow, VRP-by-trade-type) match against.
findings.why_it_matters: The low_pcr/−2 collision means the C13 router's 'contrarian × sweep-tracker: apply the penalty OR the flow read, never both' discipline is silently bypassed through the composite — the +2 line is not in the router's pair list. The sizing-floor and vocabulary drifts are classic spec-rot that make cross-file mechanical behavior depend on which file the executing agent happens to weight.
findings.confidence: high on the textual collisions; low-medium on realized impact of label drift (agents may normalize labels in practice)

findings.title: Mitigation audit: C11/C13/LB-gate close the flow-unconfirmed-accumulation hole but none addresses the core stack — C13 routes labels not points, and the LB gate REQUIRES citing 3 correlated tools to reach HIGH
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md C11/C13/LB-gate sections; daily-analysis.md Step 3a + Step 4 removed-lines comments
findings.evidence: C13's full coverage is three pairs: "multileg × vol-surface ... earnings-scout × vol-surface ... contrarian × sweep-tracker" — it routes `dominant_signal_class` ("Each idea routes to exactly one dominant_signal_class") but score_components from accumulation + DEX + OI + cum_flow + confluence still sum additively across agents on the same name. The LB gate demands "at least 3 of the 5 LOAD-BEARING tools" — all five shown above to be downstream of one actor's footprint, so the gate enforces correlated citation rather than independence. The system has pruned correlated lines before, proving the failure mode is known: "This component also double-counted with dealer-positioning's +3 DEX flip" (gamma-flip removal note) and the sweep-persistence removal — but the DEX(+3) × accumulation(+3) × OI(+1/+3) × cum_flow(+1) × confluence(+2) stack, worth 10–12 points on one footprint, survives in both rubrics.
findings.why_it_matters: Each mitigation is real but local: C11 conditions one line on one confirmer (itself correlated), C13 prevents label double-routing for three documented pairs, the LB gate prevents thin single-tool HIGHs. None introduces an independence requirement across the *quantities* (premium prints / ΔOI / DP volume / dealer-greek response are one causal chain). The honest fix the texts gesture at but never implement is a cap on total points earnable from flow-lineage components (e.g., max 6 of the 9 needed for HIGH), or requiring ≥1 non-flow confirmation (fundamentals/fz lanes are deliberately 0-point, so they can't serve).
findings.confidence: high — based entirely on the quoted mechanics of the three mitigations

things_done_well: C11 accumulation conjunction is a genuine, evidence-cited response to additive non-independence (tier inversion HIGH 60.0% < MED 62.5%, n=49) — the right diagnosis even if the confirmer is itself correlated

C2 market-excess gate is the single best protection in the system: it caps beta-longs at half regardless of score, with forward corroboration (−22pp long excess vs +20pp short) surfaced per-call so the PM sees beta vs alpha

The mechanical flow_conflict branch with explicit mutual exclusivity (−3 XOR −1, never both) fixed a measured 3-of-14 double-deduction rate — penalty-side double-counting was found and closed where it was looked for
N-conditional win-rate caps with an absolute 0.80 ceiling enforced at emission (P0.1), plus the sub-0.50 pre-emit sizing floor — quote humility is structural, not narrative

The system has a demonstrated track record of pruning correlated/negative lines (gamma-flip +2 removed explicitly for double-counting with DEX; sweep-persistence removed after two negative audits) — the audit loop does bite
Gate-output discipline requiring explicit per-call no-op verdicts makes silent gate skips auditable
Σ score_components == raw_score validator invariant with rubric-line-keyed components — score provenance is genuinely auditable
Debate is correctly bounded as cut-only ('never add it'), and the fundamentals VETO override (distribution dressed as accumulation) addresses a real microstructure blind spot
C12 liquidity floor is fail-closed with a documented denominator discipline (win-rates computed only over floor-passing names)
Advisory lanes (fz, GEX map, 0DTE setup, single-leg whale, Kelly) are rigorously held at 0 rubric points with explicit graduation gates — new signals cannot leak into the score before validation

findings.title: uw historical signal-backtest grades "5-day" wins on forward windows silently clamped to the latest bar, and the quoted win_rate is unstable under the unpinned --top-n parameter (55.6% vs 49.3% for the same class/window)
findings.where: uw CLI `historical signal-backtest` (consumed by daily-analysis.md Step 5 / weekly-analysis.md Step 5 / signal-confluence-quant.md item 2 sizing ladder)
findings.evidence: Live, 2026-06-12 pre-market (data through 06-11): `uw historical signal-backtest --signal-type bullish_flow --lookback-days 5 --top-n 20` → `"total_signals": 9, "truncated_signals": 9, "win_rate": "55.6%"` with signals ONLY from 2026-06-08/06-09. Both SNDK rows (signals 06-08 AND 06-09) show identical `price_after_5d: 1881.51`; both NVDA rows show `price_after_5d: 204.87` — which equals NVDA's 2026-06-11 close per `uw historical trend` (`{"close": 204.87, "date": "2026-06-11"}`). So the "5-day" forward return is actually 2–3 days, clamped to the last available bar, for 9-of-9 rows. Same class, same lookback, `--top-n 100` → `total: 71 truncated: 12 win_rate: 49.3%` (signals 05-14→06-09); `--top-n 10` → `{"note": "no backtest results", "total_signals": 0}`. Win-rate also decays with window: lookback 2/3/5/10 → 56.3%/52.1%/49.3%/49.3% (top-n 100). `methodology_notes`: "win_rate = fraction of signals where forward move agrees with the signal's direction. Lookback is in TRADING days; selection is positional within the yfinance bar series. In-sample backtest — not a robust live edge." Neither command file pins `--top-n`; the quant doc keys its N-cap on "the `n` field returned by uw historical signal-backtest" — no `n` field exists, only the top-n-dependent `total_signals`.
findings.why_it_matters: This number is the direct input to the Step 5 sizing ladder (≥0.70 full / 0.50–0.70 half). Under the tool's apparent default-ish parameterization the "historical win-rate" is a 9-observation, 2-session, 2–3-day momentum-continuation read of the current tape, presented as a 5-day backtest — pure recency masquerading as history. A different pagination choice moves the quote across the 0.50 sizing boundary (55.6% → 49.3% = half vs skip). Signals also span only 18 trading dates (05-14→06-09) with heavily overlapping 5-day windows, so effective independent n is a small fraction of total_signals — the N-conditional cap is keyed to an inflated denominator. The clamping additionally biases toward whatever the last 2–3 sessions did (look-ahead of the regime into the "history").
findings.confidence: high — fully reproduced live with price cross-verification against uw historical trend closes. Would soften only if the quant agent demonstrably always runs --top-n ≥100 AND drops truncated rows; nothing in any of the four files instructs either.

findings.title: "Per ticker, per signal class" win-rate is unimplementable — the CLI has no --symbol flag — and production envelopes confirm one market-wide class statistic is stamped onto every ticker, including under a class label the tool cannot even query; the flagship dark_pool_accumulation class ALWAYS returns empty and therefore permanently routes to the circular fallback
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md item 2 ("Apply per ticker, per signal class — NOT a single watchlist-wide call"); daily-analysis.md Step 5 ("Call `uw historical signal-backtest` with that signal class and the ticker"); analyses/daily/2026-06-11/decision.json
findings.evidence: `uw historical signal-backtest --help` flags: only `--lookback-days`, `--signal-type` (bullish_flow | bearish_flow | high_iv_rank | volume_spike | dark_pool_accumulation), `--top-n`. No --symbol, no --date. Live: `--signal-type dark_pool_accumulation --top-n 100` → `{"note": "no backtest results", "total_signals": 0}` (empty at every top-n). Production envelope 2026-06-11: `MU | class dealer_positioning | wr 0.479 | n 71 | src backtest`, `MRVL | ... | wr 0.479 | n 71`, `ASML | ... | wr 0.479 | n 71` — three tickers, identical market-wide quote, recorded under `dealer_positioning`, which is not a queryable --signal-type (n=71 matches the bullish_flow set exactly); `AAPL | class dark_pool_accumulation | wr 0.424 | n 85 | src fallback_proxy`.
findings.why_it_matters: The envelope's per-call `win_rate`/`win_rate_n` purport to be the ticker-and-class edge and are consumed by the sizing ladder and the calibration loop, but they are (a) a single market-wide statistic replicated across calls, (b) sometimes sourced from a *different* class than labeled (dealer_positioning ← bullish_flow), and (c) for the rubric's most heavily weighted line (+3 dark_pool_accumulation conjunction) NEVER from the backtest at all — the tool returns zero signals, so the flagship class is structurally sized by the self-referential fallback proxy every single run. Any downstream claim that "dark_pool_accumulation backtests at X%" is a measurement of the system's own past picks, not an independent signal history.

findings.title: Fallback win-rate proxy is circular and hindsight-reconstructed: it grades the system's own post-gate top-5 picks, but the watchlist stores tickers only — no direction, no signal class, no entry price — so class-matching and trade direction are re-inferred at grading time; repeated picks are pseudo-replicated in n
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md item 2 fallback (steps a–d); ~/.config/unusual-whales-pp-cli/watchlist.json; analyses/daily/2026-06-11/decision.json
findings.evidence: Fallback spec: "reading the rolling `conviction_<date>` watchlists from the last 30 calendar days (`uw watchlist manage --action list` to enumerate, then `uw historical trend --days 10` per matched ticker to grade WIN/LOSS)". Live watchlist.json: groups are bare ticker arrays — `"conviction_2026-05-18": ["MU","TSM","TTWO","MA","PLTR"]` — no direction, class, or entry field anywhere in the file. NVDA appears in ≥6 groups in the sample shown (05-11/12/13/14/15/21). `uw historical trend` returns options-flow metrics (`flow_direction`, `net_flow`, premiums) plus `close`; the fallback never defines whether WIN is graded on price or flow. Production: AAPL 06-11 `wr 0.424 | n 85 | src fallback_proxy` — ~30 days × ~5 picks/day ≈ 100 picks, 85 graded on overlapping 10-day windows.
findings.why_it_matters: Three distortion channels: (1) Selection on the gate — only top-5 post-gate, non-VETO survivors enter the graded set, so the proxy measures "how did our best-filtered picks do," then prices a NEW marginal candidate of the nominal class. (2) Hindsight direction/class — since the store carries tickers only, the grader must reconstruct what was called and which class it was, while looking at the resolved 10-day window; ambiguous picks resolve toward the outcome. (3) Procyclical feedback — sizing today's picks off the realized performance of yesterday's own picks couples position size to recent own-book P&L (inflates in trends, collapses after drawdowns); note the 06-11 proxy honestly read 0.424 in the current chop, so the bias is regime-procyclical rather than uniformly upward. Mitigations exist (0.65 cap, `low_conviction_proxy` flag, visible `win_rate_source`) but the flagship class rides this path permanently per the previous finding. Pseudo-replication (same ticker graded across overlapping windows, n=85) overstates the sample the 0.69/0.80 N-cap keys on.
findings.confidence: high on mechanism (file format and spec are verbatim); medium on magnitude — measuring the realized inflation requires comparing proxy grades against envelope-recorded directions, which lives in the quarantined audit dir.

findings.title: Weekly Step 6 thesis scorecard is graded in hindsight by the outcome-aware model, with an INCONCLUSIVE escape hatch excluded from the denominator and a week-end survivor universe — while explicitly refusing to read the verbatim daily decision envelopes that would pin the early-week calls
findings.where: weekly-analysis.md Step 6 (lines ~409–427) + §0 of the report template
findings.evidence: Verbatim: "This is derived entirely from fresh `uw` CLI queries — no daily analysis files are read." … "For every ticker surfaced by any Phase 1 agent this week, check whether signals present at the start of the week resolved in their predicted direction by week-end" … "using `covered_dates[0]` and `covered_dates[1]` as early-week reference dates" … "INCONCLUSIVE — insufficient price movement or contradictory signals (excluded from hit-rate denominator)" … "Compute the week's hit rate: wins / (wins + losses). This headline goes in the Executive Summary as Signal performance." Meanwhile the repo emits machine-readable point-in-time records daily (analyses/daily/YYYY-MM-DD/decision.json with per-call direction/tier — verified present through 2026-06-11).
findings.why_it_matters: Four channels, all but one inflationary: (1) Universe survivorship (+): the graded set is "tickers surfaced by Phase 1 agents this week," but Phase 1 runs at week-end on persistence-ranked tools — names whose Monday signal collapsed mid-week drop out of week-end screens and never enter the denominator as losses. (2) Hindsight direction (+): "early-week direction" is reconstructed from day-1/2 flow data queried on Friday by a model that already sees Friday's tape; ambiguous flow gets labeled with the direction that resolved. (3) Denominator exclusion (+): losers almost always exhibit "contradictory signals" by Friday, so the INCONCLUSIVE clause preferentially absorbs would-be LOSSes out of wins/(wins+losses). (4) Conjunctive WIN (−, weak): WIN requires flow AND price confirmation, which pushes mixed rows not to LOSS but to INCONCLUSIVE — i.e. channel 4 feeds channel 3 rather than offsetting it. Net sign: inflates the Executive-Summary headline hit rate by an unbounded, discretionary amount. The fix is sitting on disk: grade against the prior week's decision.json calls[] (ticker, direction, tier pinned ex-ante) — the "no daily files" rule was meant to avoid stale-data dependency but instead converts a verifiable scorecard into self-graded reconstruction.
findings.confidence: high on structure (verbatim spec); medium on realized magnitude — quantifying requires comparing §0 tables to envelope calls, and past audit comparisons are quarantined for this run.

findings.title: C2 market-excess benchmark: "same-direction SPY over the same windows" is not reconstructible from the tool's output, and for the freshest signals the nominal windows extend into the future; clustered overlapping windows make the binary excess gate a single noisy regime draw
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md "Market-excess gate (2026-05-25 register C2)"; scripts/excess_winrate.py market_excess/size_decision
findings.evidence: Spec: "benchmark = the same-direction SPY bet over the same signal windows as the class's `uw historical signal-backtest` … Compute it from a dedicated SPY `uw historical trend` over the same dates." Live tool output exposes only `signal_date` and `price_after_5d` — never the window end-date — and the windows are clamped (06-09 signals end 06-11, 2 trading days, per the price_after_5d ≡ last-close evidence above). An agent reconstructing "signal_date + 5 trading days" for the 06-08/06-09 signals lands on 06-15/06-16 — dates that do not exist yet at the 06-12 pre-market run. The 5-day signal set is 71 signals over 18 consecutive dates (overlapping windows); SPY itself appears INSIDE the bullish_flow signal set (`"ticker": "SPY", "signal_date": "2026-06-09"` row) along with QQQ/NDX/IWM/SMH/SOXX. `excess_winrate.py:market_excess` is pure arithmetic — `signal_win_rate - benchmark_win_rate` — window construction is entirely on the agent.
findings.why_it_matters: The gate concept is sound and load-bearing (their own audit found longs −22pp excess), but its measurement is fragile in exactly the look-ahead dimension: (a) signal-side WR is computed on clamped 2–3-day windows while the SPY benchmark is computed on whatever windows the agent can actually build — apples-to-oranges excess, sign-flippable near the 0 boundary where the gate is binary (cap-at-half vs no-cap). (b) Overlapping clustered windows mean the "benchmark over the same windows" is essentially one draw of the current leg — the gate fires or no-ops on noise. (c) Index/ETF rows inside the signal class numerator drag the class WR toward SPY mechanically, biasing measured excess toward 0 from the signal side — the doc's anti-double-count warning covers only the benchmark side. Note the windows-cluster-in-up-legs effect (bullish_flow fires in rallies → high SPY benchmark → longs capped) is the gate working as designed, not a bug.
findings.confidence: medium-high — window non-reconstructibility and clamping are verified live; whether agents in practice truncate SPY windows consistently with the tool's clamp is unobservable from the spec (nothing instructs it).

findings.title: Liquidity floor (C12) is evaluated as-of-today against historical signal rows, and the tool's headline class rates are NOT floored — sub-$5 names sit inside the emitted vol_realisation_rate, and the tool freely emits rates (94.4%) above the 0.80 ceiling that only agent discipline keeps out of the envelope
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md "Liquidity floor on the win-rate denominator (C12)"; scripts/excess_winrate.py passes_liquidity_floor/_candidates_from_json; uw historical signal-backtest volume_spike/high_iv_rank output
findings.evidence: Live: `--signal-type volume_spike --top-n 100` → `vol_realisation_rate: 62.0%` with first row `{"ticker": "CLSZ", "price_on_signal": 4.62, ...}` — below the $5 MIN_PRICE floor, inside the headline rate. `--signal-type high_iv_rank --top-n 100` → `vrr: 94.4%` (vs the 0.80 ABSOLUTE_WR_CEILING). `excess_winrate.py` Candidate takes `price`/`adv_usd` supplied by the agent ("come from yahoo or a screener field") — backtest rows carry no ADV and no historical price/volume context, so flooring historical rows necessarily uses TODAY's price/ADV. The floor is fail-closed on missing data.
findings.why_it_matters: Two denominator-regime problems: (1) Time-inconsistent flooring — a name's floor status is evaluated at audit/quote time, not signal time. Names that collapsed below $5/$50M (typically after losing signals) drop out of the class history with their losses; names that grew into liquidity (typically after winning) stay in with their wins — a survivorship tilt that inflates long-class win-rates, the same mechanism as index-membership look-ahead. (2) Emission-path risk — the C12 instruction requires the agent to hand-recompute the class rate over floored rows with externally fetched ADV per row (≈70 yahoo lookups), while the un-floored, un-capped headline (62.0%, 94.4%) is one field away. The 94.4% high_iv_rank headline is exactly the shape of quote the vol-lane previously leaked (per the stale-cap memory note); the tool still serves it, so the ceiling binds only at the prompt layer. (3) The fallback proxy's 30-day pick window also spans pre-C12 picks (groups exist from conviction_2026-05-11; floor shipped 05-25), mixing floored and un-floored selection regimes in one denominator.
findings.confidence: high for the un-floored/un-capped headlines (verbatim live rows); medium for the survivorship magnitude — the 33-name current signal universe is all mega-caps, so the bias is latent rather than currently binding, but the volume_spike/high_iv_rank classes hit it today.

findings.title: Watchlist write-back feedback loop: largely well-contained, but the backtest tool's own signal universe overlaps 21/33 with the system's past picks — the "independent" backtest path and the self-grading fallback path measure substantially the same attention set
findings.where: daily-analysis.md Step 8 / weekly-analysis.md Step 9 (write-back); risk-monitor.md items 7, 8, 12; live watchlist.json vs signal-backtest universe
findings.evidence: Live: bullish_flow signal universe (top-n 100) = 33 tickers; intersection with the watchlist union = 21 (`['AAPL','AMD','AMZN','ASTS','AVGO','IWM','META','MRVL','MSFT','MU','NEE','NVDA','ORCL','PANW','PLTR','QQQ','SMH','SNDK','SPY','STM','TSLA']`). watchlist.json union `tickers` list has grown to 60+ names and conviction groups accrue daily (06-10, 06-11, week groups W20–W23 present). risk-monitor.md item 5: correlation is run "on today's candidate tickers (not the static watchlist)". Items 7/8: alerts/scan run against yesterday's group for exit candidates only; item 12 writes today's top-5 back.
findings.why_it_matters: The loop is mostly defused where it counts: correlation/risk runs on today's candidates, the alerts channel is exit-only (can't promote), and the debate/gates are cut-only. The residual self-reinforcement channels are (a) the fallback proxy (covered above) and (b) a subtler one: because both the uw backtest's signal detection and the system's funnel condition on the same flow leaderboards, "backtest win_rate" — even via the nominal non-fallback path — is largely the trailing performance of the same mega-cap attention set the system has been picking, so it partially re-measures the system's own recent book either way. Also note Step 0's funnel conditioning (top-25 movers / ≥3x volume / net-premium leaders) guarantees entries are post-extreme-move while the backtest grades from T-close — combined with the overnight-gap point below, measured class WR refers to systematically better entries than a post-market pipeline can take (live entry is T+1 open; the T-close→T+1-open drift after a big flow day is captured by the backtest but not by the desk). Sign: inflates transferable edge for momentum classes; mixes reversal into fade-class measurements.
findings.confidence: high on the overlap and loop structure (live data); medium on the overnight-gap magnitude — entry-at-T-close is verified (price_on_signal == T close for NVDA/SNDK/SPY against trend closes) but the gap premium itself was not measured in this audit.

things_done_well: The C2 market-excess gate is conceptually exactly right and downgrade-only: 'beta cannot masquerade as edge', benchmark from a dedicated SPY trend with an explicit anti-double-count warning ('Do NOT reuse SPY's appearance inside the signal class's own backtest set'), corroborated by their own −22pp long-book finding. It is the single best structural defense against the up-tape look-ahead this lens hunts for — the criticisms above are about its measurement, not its design.

Win-rate humility machinery binds at emission and is visible: 0.69 cap below n=10, 0.80 absolute ceiling at any n, sub-0.50 ⇒ starter/skip pre-emit check, 'never emit 1.00', and the raw n + uncapped rate preserved in audit_trail. The production envelope honestly records `win_rate_source: fallback_proxy` — the fallback is flagged, capped at 0.65, and carries `low_conviction_proxy`, so its circularity is at least not hidden.

The tool's own methodology_notes say 'In-sample backtest — not a robust live edge' — the data layer is honest about itself, and the command files repeatedly propagate 'advisory, 0 rubric points' framing for unvalidated lanes (GEX map, 0DTE, fz, C19 single-leg).

Σ score_components == raw_score is a validator-enforced invariant with rubric-line-keyed components and named source agent + tool per point — the score is genuinely auditable, which is what made this audit's production cross-check possible at all.

Mechanical gate discipline: explicit per-call gate_verdicts even on no-op, mechanical correlation thresholds (≥0.70 / 0.60–0.70 / <0.60) replacing discretion, mutually-exclusive flow_conflict switch written as executable pseudocode, and debate/fundamentals/event gates that can only cut size, never add.

The feedback loop's most dangerous channel was already closed: portfolio-correlation runs on today's candidate union, not the static watchlist, and watchlist alerts are exit-only. The decision.json envelope architecture (point-in-time, machine-readable, validated) is the correct de-look-ahead substrate — the weekly Step 6 just declines to use it.

Liquidity floor is fail-closed with a tested stdlib helper, and the funnel/denominator are explicitly tied together ('the floored set is the funnel every downstream step consumes') — the time-inconsistency is a refinement gap, not a design absence.

findings.title: Every live promote/demote decision except (possibly) one was made on a marginal-contribution estimate whose 95% CI straddles zero
findings.where: daily-analysis.md Step 4 rubric changelog comments (lines 295–311); weekly-analysis.md Step 4 (lines 354–368); signal-confluence-quant.md P1.1/P0.3 sections
findings.evidence: Cited bases: "+27.8pp marginal contribution (LOAD-BEARING)" (accumulation +2→+3); "marginal contribution −23pp (n=8)" (conviction-matrix gated to LEAP-only); "+19.5pp marginal contribution (n=12, LOAD-BEARING)" (signal-confluence +2 AND added to the 3-of-5 HIGH gate); "marginal contribution −22pp two consecutive audits (n=15)" / "−24pp marginal, n=13" (sweep-persistence removed). Computed 95% CIs for a difference-in-win-rates at the stated n (baseline complement generously n=40): conviction-matrix −23pp → [−0.588, +0.128]; signal-confluence +19.5pp → [−0.096, +0.486]; sweep-persistence −22pp → [−0.504, +0.064] and −24pp → [−0.535, +0.055]; sector-persist +2.8pp → [−0.266, +0.322]. ALL straddle zero. Only accumulation +27.8pp (n unstated; assumed 15) marginally excludes zero [+0.033, +0.523] — and it was measured in the same 2026-05-15 Phase 4, same close-only grading, that produced cum_flow's +24.2pp, which the 2026-06-06 audit itself ruled "a close-only-method artifact" and demoted +3→+1 ("NO-INFO across three consecutive path-aware audits (−3.5pp MC)"). Minimum detectable effect at 95%: ±34.6pp at n=8, ±28.3pp at n=12, ±25.3pp at n=15 — at or above every cited effect.
findings.why_it_matters: The rubric weights are being retuned each cycle on point estimates that are statistically indistinguishable from noise, then frozen into the prompt as established facts ("LOAD-BEARING"). The cum_flow whipsaw (+2→+3 on +24.2pp, then +3→+1 as a measurement artifact) is a realized false positive proving the mechanism. The signal-confluence case is the most consequential: an insignificant n=12 reading earned it +2 points AND membership in the 3-of-5 gate that decides which calls may full-size. The sweep removal is the most defensible (two same-sign replications), but the two samples come from overlapping report windows, so they are not independent replications. Mitigation that keeps this at P1 not P0: most decisions were demotions/conditionalizations (risk-reducing direction), and the downgrade-only cap stack bounds live damage.
findings.confidence: high on the CI math (stated n taken at face value; exact complement-set sizes unverifiable without opening quarantined audit files). Would change my mind: audit files showing the pp figures came from pooled multi-week samples materially larger than the quoted n, or that BH-corrected p-values accompanied the pre-05-30 decisions.

findings.title: Non-stationary measurement loop: rubric version AND outcome-grading method both change every cycle, so the cross-audit series used to justify changes is not comparable — and the envelope records no rubric version
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md Tier cuts paragraph (line 127); daily-analysis.md line 333; schemas/decision_envelope.schema.json
findings.evidence: The HIGH-cut justification chains three numbers from three different (rubric, grading) regimes as if one series: "2026-05-29 (close-only) score-9 realised 0.70 (n=10); 2026-05-30 (path-aware) the ≥9 HIGH bin realised 0.774 (n=31)" superseding "the 2026-05-15 ≥10 cut (set because its smaller close-only sample showed ≥9 realised 0.667)". Meanwhile the same 06-06 audit invalidated a close-only-era promotion: "Original promotion (+2→+3, 2026-05-15, +24.2pp) was a close-only-method artifact." Each audit also changes the rubric that generates the next dataset (C11 conjunction + 3-of-5 gate reshaped which names score ≥9 after 05-23). Live probe: grep of schemas/decision_envelope.schema.json shows "schema_version": {"enum": ["1.0", "1.1", "1.2"]} — versions the envelope shape only; no rubric_version field exists, and project memory confirms era-banding must be inferred ("envelopes 2026-05-30→06-05 record raw-9 calls as MEDIUM (era-banded; do not rewrite; audits must read accordingly)").
findings.why_it_matters: Scores produced under rubric v3 are graded (under grading method m2) to retune rubric v4 — the classic moving-target problem: apparent improvement across audits (0.667→0.70→0.774) can be produced entirely by methodology drift plus selection, with zero change in real edge. Because the envelope carries no rubric_version, future audits cannot mechanically stratify calls by rubric era and will silently pool heterogeneous regimes — exactly how the close-only artifact entered in the first place. Fix is cheap: add rubric_version (and grading_method) to the envelope top level.
findings.confidence: high — the version confounding is verbatim in the files and the missing field is verified by live grep. Would change my mind: a frozen-rubric replay harness in the audit skill that re-scores historical candidate unions under each rubric version (I could not check the quarantined audit dirs for one).

findings.title: Tier bands are at material risk of being a threshold-snooping artifact: HIGH cut moved 5→10→9 chasing in-sample bins, the triggering 'tier inversion' was itself insignificant, holdout had zero resolved HIGH — and the single-regime assumption broke today
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md lines 118–139; daily-analysis.md lines 324–333, Step 3a; weekly-analysis.md line 389
findings.evidence: File self-admission: "⚠ In-sample-only — re-confirm at the ~2026-06-12 audit: the 2026-05-30 holdout had 0 resolved HIGH calls and the dataset is a single UPTREND regime." The 05-23 re-architecture (C11 conjunction + 3-of-5 gate) was triggered by "tier inversion (HIGH 60.0% < MED 62.5%, n=49)" — at bin sizes ~25/24 that is a −2.5pp difference, 95% CI [−0.298, +0.248]: pure noise treated as a P0 defect. The fix's validation: "Phase 5 W21 holdout shows the 3-of-5 gate restores tier monotonicity (HIGH 0.80 / MED 0.50 / LOW 0.50)" — HIGH 0.80 at plausible n=5 (4/5) has Wilson CI [0.376, 0.964], indistinguishable from a coin flip. The current ≥9 cut rests on 0.774 (n=31), Wilson CI [0.602, 0.886], in-sample, cut chosen after seeing the bins. Live probe (uw risk market-regime, 2026-06-11 EOD): "regime": "TRANSITIONAL — Mixed signals...", "trend": "PULLBACK_IN_UPTREND", SPY above_20sma: false — the regime is no longer the UPTREND every band was fit on, as of the exact re-confirm date.
findings.why_it_matters: Moving a decision threshold to whichever bin boundary restores monotonicity in the current sample is textbook threshold snooping — with ~30 obs per bin the 'optimal' cut wanders ±1 point cycle to cycle by chance. Worse, the cycle began by 'fixing' an inversion that was never statistically there. The stated safety net ("a score-9 beta-long promoted to HIGH is still capped at half by the C2 market-excess gate") is real but was itself measured only in the UPTREND; the −22pp-longs/+20pp-shorts excess structure is regime-conditional almost by definition and is now untested in the TRANSITIONAL tape it just entered.
findings.confidence: high on the snooping mechanics and the live regime flip; medium on the W21 holdout n (0.80 strongly suggests 4/5 but the exact denominator lives in quarantined audit files). Would change my mind: tier monotonicity holding on a genuinely frozen out-of-sample window with n≥30 resolved HIGH across ≥2 regimes.

findings.title: Gate-stack compression: 8 stacked −1-tier risk gates on a 4-level size scale, on top of 3 quant caps that already cap all longs at half — expected modal final size for a long is starter/skip, so conviction tiers no longer differentiate realized sizing
findings.where: risk-monitor.md 'Sizing rule' (lines 43–54) + gates 5/9/10/11; signal-confluence-quant.md C2/C4/N-cap sections; daily-analysis.md Step 5
findings.evidence: risk-monitor stacks VETO plus eight −1-tier gates (regime, panic, VRP, cluster, sector, fundamentals-CAUTION, event-risk, debate) onto a full/half/starter/skip scale, after the quant's downgrade-only N-cap, market-excess cap, and C4 opening cap. The 05-30 audit found "every long-side class is negative-excess beta" (−22pp), so C2 caps essentially every long at half pre-risk. Poisson-binomial over the 8 gates at plausible firing rates (regime .10, panic .05, VRP .15, cluster .25, sector .10, CAUTION .20, event_risk .40 post-re-scope, debate .40): P(0 fire)=0.14, P(1)=0.34, P(≥2)=0.52 → final-size distribution for a modal long: half 14%, starter 34%, skip 52%. The system already ran this experiment once: the pre-re-scope event-risk gate "fired on 90% of post-register calls (47/52) while its downgrades realised exactly the ungated win-rate (43% vs 43%)" — the file's own verdict: "A gate that taxes everything equally is a haircut, not a filter."
findings.why_it_matters: If HIGH and MEDIUM both overwhelmingly resolve to starter/skip after gating, the tier label — the variable the entire audit-and-retune enterprise optimizes — is decoupled from realized capital at risk. The meta-process is then tuning a cosmetic variable: weight changes justified by ±20pp marginal contributions move scores that move tiers that barely move size. It also starves the calibration loop's own activation gates (C3 Kelly needs tier×expectancy monotonicity on n≥30 closed calls; uniform starter sizing yields no per-tier P&L differentiation worth the name). The event_risk episode is empirical proof the stack's marginal gate can be a pure tax with zero discrimination — and seven other gates have never had their discrimination measured (only event_risk has a published firing-rate/discrimination check).
findings.confidence: medium-high — the gate enumeration and the event_risk natural experiment are verbatim; the firing-rate assumptions for the other seven gates are mine (flagged): even halving them leaves P(≥1 gate) ≈ 0.6. Would change my mind: an envelope-level tally showing realized final_size actually varies materially by tier (e.g. HIGH names ending full/half ≥50% of the time).

findings.title: Weekly thin-window rule lowers the HIGH bar (≥9 → 8+) exactly when evidence is thinnest — evidence-threshold loosening with no compensating size cap, and thin-window HIGHs enter future calibration bins unmarked
findings.where: weekly-analysis.md 'Failure modes & recovery' (line 557)
findings.evidence: "`uw historical available-dates` shows fewer than 3 covered weekdays — produce a 'limited-data weekly' with that explicit caveat in the Executive Summary, and downgrade tier thresholds (HIGH = 8+, MEDIUM = 6–7, LOW = 3–5) for the smaller window. (Downgrade preserves the same relative gap to the 2026-05-30 default cuts of HIGH ≥9 / MED 7–8 / LOW 3–6.)" The points being renormalized away are precisely the persistence lines the same file calls the edge ("+3 uw historical oi-trend BUILDING for the full week, --days ≥ 5"; "+2 multileg ... repeated on ≥2 days"). No accompanying sizing haircut appears in the rule, and the decision-envelope spec (Step 10) defines no thin-window flag on calls[] — the caveat is Executive-Summary prose only.
findings.why_it_matters: Statistically backwards: fewer covered days = wider uncertainty on every persistence read, so the defensible response is a higher confluence bar or a hard size cap, not a lower score cut that preserves the production rate of HIGH labels. The 'same relative gap' argument renormalizes the score arithmetic but not the evidence content — an 8 scored on 2 days is a weaker evidence class than a 9 on 5 days, yet both inherit the HIGH full-size default and, because nothing in the envelope marks the thin window, both pool into the same ≥9/HIGH bins at the next tier-calibration audit, quietly degrading the very statistics used to set the bands.
findings.confidence: high on the mechanism (rule text and envelope spec are verbatim; weekly notes carry more capital per the file's own ≥5 confluence rationale). Would change my mind: if in practice thin-window weeks always also trip a size cap elsewhere, or if the audit skill demonstrably excludes limited-data weeklies from tier calibration.

findings.title: Multiple testing without correction for the decisions that are still live: ~90 component-level looks plus dozens of tuned thresholds against ≤~150 overlapping resolved observations in one regime; BH arrived 2026-05-30, after most surviving weights were set
findings.where: Step 4 rubrics (both commands) — ~15 changelog-annotated components across 6 audit cycles (2026-05-09/15/23/25/30/06-06); signal-confluence-quant.md withheld-lines section

'Two consecutive audits' replications (sweep −24pp/−22pp) draw from overlapping report windows — not independent confirmations.
findings.why_it_matters: With the number of effective tuned parameters approaching the number of independent resolved observations, the rubric is at or past the overfit boundary by construction: selecting the largest of ~15 noisy contrasts each cycle guarantees impressive-looking pp figures regardless of true edge (Harvey-Liu-Zhu / deflated-Sharpe logic). The good news — withheld lines C6/C8 show the post-05-30 process now demands gates before shipping — does not retroactively launder the pre-BH weights, which is where most of the current rubric's mass sits.
findings.confidence: medium-high — look-count is an estimate from the changelog density (flagged); the BH timing comes from project memory rather than quarantined audit files. Would change my mind: evidence that pre-05-30 decisions were re-tested under the BH+N≥8 regime and re-affirmed (the 06-06 cum_flow demotion suggests re-testing happens, but selectively).

findings.title: Persistence doctrine ('single-day signals are noise; multi-day persistence is the edge') is contradicted by the system's own measurements, yet still silently shapes the candidate funnel where the audit loop cannot falsify it
findings.where: daily-analysis.md 'Operating principle' (line 40); weekly-analysis.md lines 62–75; Step 4 rubrics; C19 sections
findings.evidence: Doctrine: "Single-day signals are noise; multi-day persistence is the edge. Pass this instruction through to every spawned agent." Versus their own audit record: the most literal persistence signal was removed ("swept on ≥3 of 5 days REMOVED... marginal contribution −22pp two consecutive audits"); cum-premium-flow accretion demoted to +1 as "NO-INFO across three consecutive path-aware audits"; sector persistence "standalone is NO-INFO at +2.8pp"; daily oi-trend demoted +2→+1 ("supportive, not load-bearing"). Meanwhile the best validated edge in the repo is a single-print signal: "Tier-1 opening put WR 63.5% (+26pp vs SPY, p<0.001)" (single-leg whale, one ticket, one day). What the audits found actually carries: cross-tool/cross-agent confluence (signal-confluence +19.5pp, the C11 conjunction) — breadth of agreement, not time persistence.
findings.why_it_matters: Load-bearing vs decorative: the doctrine is decorative in the rubric (its scored expressions keep getting deleted) but load-bearing in the funnel — it dictates which tools agents lead with and therefore which candidates ever reach scoring. That placement makes it unfalsifiable inside the calibration loop: names suppressed for being 'only' single-day signals never enter the book, so no audit can measure the doctrine's cost. The C19 result is direct evidence the suppressed class contains the strongest edge found to date. The doctrine should be restated as 'cross-source confluence is the edge' or itself put under a measurement gate.
findings.confidence: high on the internal contradiction (all quotes verbatim); medium on materiality — persistence may still earn its keep as a funnel-stage false-positive filter, which is precisely the untested claim. Would change my mind: an A/B funnel audit admitting single-day candidates and comparing realized hit rates.

findings.title: 0.69/0.80 emission caps: directionally justified humility, but implemented as a hard winsorization with an 11pp cliff at n=10 that crosses the full-size line, and 0.69 is a sizing rule masquerading as a probability
findings.where: signal-confluence-quant.md calibration rules (lines 46–53); scripts/excess_winrate.py line 128
findings.evidence: Justification is real reliability data, not vibes: "the 0.80–0.90 quote bucket realised 62%, the ≥0.90 bucket realised 53% — overconfidence is localized entirely to the high tail." So the lens-question's hypothetical (a genuinely-0.93 class mispriced at 0.80) has no empirical instance — on their own diagram nothing realises above ~0.62 from the high tail. Implementation, verified live: `cap = 0.69 if n < 10 else ABSOLUTE_WR_CEILING` (0.80) — one additional observation (n=9→10) legally moves the quote 0.69→0.80, jumping across the 0.70 full-size ladder line, so full-size eligibility can hinge on a single sample. And 0.69 is explicitly reverse-engineered against the ladder, not estimated: "0.69 sits one notch below the full line, capping a single-regime small-N class at half" — the emitted 'win_rate' is a control variable, no longer an estimate of anything.
findings.why_it_matters: Two distortions: (1) point masses at 0.69/0.80 in the emitted quotes degrade future reliability diagrams (the 0.80 bucket now conflates genuine-0.80 classes with capped-0.9x classes, so the audit loses the ability to detect whether the high tail ever becomes real); (2) the n=10 cliff creates a discontinuous sizing incentive at exactly the sample sizes the live tool returns (probed: n=7,7,9,10). A Wilson/Jeffreys lower bound (e.g. quote the 1-sided 80% LB) achieves the same humility smoothly, keeps the quote an estimator, and removes the cliff. Mitigant already in place: raw WR + n are preserved in audit_trail, so this is recoverable.
findings.confidence: high — code and rationale verbatim, cliff verified in excess_winrate.py. Would change my mind on severity: if a class near n=10 is shown flip-flopping across the cliff in successive envelopes (would raise to P1).

statProcess.lens: LENS 3 — Statistical process / overfitting to own audits (market-maker quant / buy-side PM perspective)
live_probes_run: python3 (binomial Wilson/diff-CI computations + Poisson-binomial gate-stack size distribution — script in transcript)
things_done_well: Downgrade-only architecture throughout: every cap and gate can only cut size, never add it — the failure mode of a noise-fit weight is a missed trade, not a blown-up one. The C2 market-excess gate in particular (beta cannot masquerade as edge) is genuinely sophisticated, was confirmed by forward data (−22pp long excess / +20pp short excess), and is computed correctly: raw uncapped WR on both sides, dedicated SPY trend benchmark, explicit warning against reusing SPY from inside the class set.

Real self-correction: the system demotes its own promotions when evidence reverses (cum_flow +3→+1 as a 'close-only-method artifact'), withdraws failed half-measures ('mega-cap suppression rule... was insufficient'), and re-scopes over-firing gates based on measured gate effectiveness (event_risk: 90% firing, 43%-vs-43% discrimination). Measuring gate firing-rate vs discrimination at all is rarer than it should be on real desks.

Audit-trail discipline is excellent: rubric-line-keyed score_components, the Σ points == raw_score invariant enforced by a validator, mandatory explicit no-op gate verdicts ('absence of a verdict reads as didn't check'), and win_rate_n / win_rate_source serialized into the envelope so audits can weight by sample quality.
Raw uncapped win_rate + n preserved in audit_trail with the cap applied only at emission — the underlying data survives for later recalibration, so the winsorization is reversible.

Honest self-labelling of in-sample status where it matters: '⚠ In-sample-only (holdout had 0 resolved HIGH), single UPTREND regime — re-confirm ~2026-06-12' appears verbatim in three files; the backtest tool's own payload says 'In-sample backtest — not a robust live edge'; the 0DTE advisory explicitly flags the unsampled short-vol tail.

Advisory quarantine with pre-registered graduation gates: C19 single-leg (held at 0 points pending ≥60 days / ≥2 regimes despite p<0.001), C3 Kelly (n≥30 tier×expectancy monotone), C28 distribution_flag (≥10pp on n≥15), C6/C8 withheld with explicit numeric bars (split ≥10pp on n≥15). Pre-registering activation thresholds is the correct antidote to the very overfitting this lens audits — the newer process is converging on sound inference even where legacy weights predate it.
Denominator hygiene: the C12 liquidity floor applied fail-closed to the win-rate denominator, and the C13 mutually-exclusive signal-class routing with a 0-double-count acceptance criterion.
